title: Lesson 1: print()
lessonSummary: Your first call has rung out! With print() you put everything on the screen.

tasks.instruction: Run this example and look at the output below.
tasks.codeTemplate:
print("Hello at the riding ranch!")
print("Welcome to Sunny Valley!")

# An empty line makes things easier to read
print()
print("=== YOUR RIDING BEGINS ===")

tasks.instruction: Use print() to output a greeting of your own that contains the word "ranch".

title: Lesson 2: Variables
lessonSummary: Perfect! Variables let you keep values and change them later.

tasks.instruction: Run this example. It shows text and number variables.
tasks.codeTemplate:
horse_name = "Bobby"   # Text (String)
horse_age = 5          # Number (Integer)

print(horse_name)
print(horse_age)

tasks.instruction: Store the text "Sunny Valley" in a variable called ranch and print the variable with print().
Create a variable feed with the value 2. Then change it to 3 and print feed.

title: Lesson 3: Joining Texts
lessonSummary: Exactly how you build whole sentences from texts and numbers – don't forget str() for numbers!

tasks.instruction: Run this example – notice where str() is needed.
tasks.codeTemplate:
name = "Stormy"
breed = "Haflinger"
age = 8

print("Horse: " + name)
print("Age: " + str(age) + " years")
print(name + " is a " + breed + " and " + str(age) + " years old.")

validation.expected: Stormy is a Haflinger and 8 years old.

tasks.instruction: Create a variable age with the value 5 and use + and str() to print exactly this text: Age: 5

title: Lesson 4: input()
lessonSummary: Now your program can talk to people – input() makes it interactive.

tasks.instruction: Run this example. An input window opens – enter a horse's name there.
tasks.codeTemplate:
horse = input("What is your horse's name? ")
print("Welcome to the ranch, " + horse + "!")

tasks.instruction: Use input() to ask for your rider's name, store the answer in rider and print: I ride with: (followed by the name)

title: Lesson 5: Comments
lessonSummary: Comments are your stable notes – Python ignores them, but they help you find your way around your code.

tasks.instruction: Run this example. Notice which line is NOT executed.
tasks.codeTemplate:
# This line prints the horse's name
print("Bobby")

print("5 years old")  # shows the horse's age

print("This will run")
# print("This will NOT run")

tasks.instruction: Write a comment of your own and then a print() that outputs exactly: Comment read
